title: Cross-SDK retry playbook: pragmatic backoff defaults, idempotency semantics, and streaming resume guidance
creator: Marco Nguyen
description:
Problem: SDK consumers across Python/TypeScript/Go are seeing inconsistent retry behavior and unclear idempotency contracts when an inference request fails or is partially served. Streaming endpoints introduce additional complexity: some clients want automatic resume, others want deterministic duplicate suppression.

Goal: Deliver a concise cross-SDK playbook that defines safe, pragmatic defaults for retries and backoff, a small and obvious idempotency key contract for non-streamed calls, and guidance/utility primitives for streaming resume semantics. Provide language-specific examples and one-liner recipes that are safe for product teams to adopt without deep protocol knowledge.

Scope and deliverables:
- Consensus default presets for simple requests and for long-running/streaming requests (per-language).
- Clear idempotency key behavior: when to require, server expectations, suggested client UUID approach, and examples.
- Retryable error taxonomy mapped to HTTP/gRPC codes and gateway error strings (network, transient infra, quota, model OOM, rate limit).
- Streaming semantics: resume token model, best-effort resume vs restart, and API ergonomics for each SDK.
- Minimal example snippets in Python, TypeScript, and Go demonstrating: attach idempotency key, configure default retry policy, and resume a streaming response.
- Backwards compatibility notes and migration checklist for products using existing SDKs.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Engineering sign-off on taxonomy and default numbers (base backoff, multiplier, max attempts, jitter strategy).
2) Language owners have approved ergonomic surfaces and example snippets.
3) Unit and integration tests for default retry behavior across SDKs added in sdks-2025.03 pipeline.
4) Documentation page and quickstart snippet published to SDK docs.

Notes on trade-offs: we bias to a conservative default to avoid silent duplication for high-value operations. For high-throughput, low-value calls we document an opt-in low-latency preset. Streaming resume introduces statefulness on server; defaults should be "best-effort resume" with explicit opt-in for durable resume semantics.
comments: 2025-02-18 Marco Nguyen: Created ticket after sync with product. Initial scoping focused on three items: defaults, idempotency contract, streaming guidance. Linked design doc stub (confluence).

2025-02-20 Aisha Patel: Drafted first-pass defaults: simple request preset = {base=100ms, multiplier=2.0, max_attempts=4, jitter=full}; aggressive preset = {base=25ms, multiplier=1.6, max_attempts=3, jitter=small}. Proposed that SDKs expose RetryPolicy object with .apply(preset).

2025-02-22 Ruth Kim (review): Concern about default max_attempts on large generation requests (tokens consumed). Suggested server-side duplicate suppression via idempotency key for any request that may have side effects. Recommended explicit opt-in for 'at-most-once' behaviour where cost matters.

2025-02-25 Sven Larsen (infra): Ran latency/resilience experiments against staging runtime. Summary: for small requests (<=128 tokens) the conservative preset reduced errors by 43% at cost of 4% median latency. Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/latency/retry-tests. Added numbers to design doc.

2025-02-27 Aisha Patel: Defined idempotency contract: clients SHOULD send Idempotency-Key header (UUIDv4). Server will dedupe identical keys for 24h for synchronous non-streamed generation endpoints. Streaming endpoints will accept Resume-Token returned in event stream; SDKs should surface resume token and helper to retry with resume. Draft examples added to PR.

2025-03-01 Marco Nguyen: Discussed streaming resume with API team — tradeoff matrix documented. Choice: default = best-effort resume using resume tokens (stateless on server if possible), durable resume (full guarantee) behind feature flag and explicit request param. Recording: https://meet.redwood.ai/rec/stream-resume-20250301.

2025-03-03 Aisha Patel: Opened language PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1298 (python), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1301 (ts), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1307 (go). Each PR adds RetryPolicy presets, IdempotencyKey helper, and a streaming resume example.

2025-03-04 QA feedback (Elena Ortiz): Found edge case when retries interact with per-request server-side rate-limit tokens. Added fallback: when server returns 429 with 'Retry-After', SDK respects server header and bypasses client backoff multiplier for that attempt. Added test case.

2025-03-05 Marco Nguyen: Consolidated examples in docs and linked Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/SDK+Retry+Playbook. Next: language owners to finish API ergonomics review and we will land PRs by 2025-03-12.
